facts.value: 1530s, break with papal jurisdiction under Henry VIII

citations.excerpt: In the 1530s the English church rejected the jurisdiction of the Bishop of Rome and came under Lutheran and then Calvinist theological influences.

The Church of England emerged as a distinct Western Christian ecclesial tradition in the early 16th century, when King Henry VIII declared his supremacy over the English church and its independence from papal authority.
The parliament of 1529 lasted until 1536; it broke the bonds of Rome, established royal supremacy over the English Church
In the 1530s the English church rejected the jurisdiction of the Bishop of Rome

facts.value: Retained bishops, the threefold ministry and much medieval structure while adopting a vernacular Bible and reformed liturgy. Identity shaped by the Book of Common Prayer and the Thirty-nine Articles.

citations.excerpt: The threefold ministry, ordination by bishops, the diocesan-parochial structure, cathedrals, church courts and much medieval canon law were retained.
The English Bible, the Book of Common Prayer, the Christian Year, the parochial context and loyalty to the sovereign gave the Church of England a distinct identity.

facts.value: The established church of England. The Elizabethan settlement restored royal authority over the church, with the sovereign as Supreme Governor. It is governed by a general synod of bishops, clergy and laity.

citations.excerpt: An Act of Supremacy restored to the crown the authority over the church held by Henry VIII.
It is governed by a general synod of bishops, clergy and laity.
Elizabeth rejected the title of Supreme Head, and used that of Supreme Governor
while remaining the established church and continuing to value partnership with the state.
